lines: Keep clear of the stonecutter. It does not care who started the conversation.
Give the stonecutter room. It is sharper than this conversation needs to be.
Stand wide of the stonecutter. It never asks who leaned in first.
There you are. I was just near the stonecutter, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Mind the dust. It travels better than most merchants.
Hello. Stand clear of the stone unless you know where it wants to fall.
You caught me between measurements.
Careful near the cutter. It has no patience for fingers.
Good timing. The mortar is resting and so am I, briefly.
Come closer, but not under that block.
I have a moment before the next corner demands proof.
Welcome. If you lean on that stack, we both learn something bad.
The stone is steady today. I appreciate the example.
Speak up. The chisel has been arguing with me.
Hello there. Try not to kick the guide line.
I was checking level. People are harder to keep straight.
Stand where the floor is finished and tell me what you need.
Good to see you arriving without loose rubble.
The wall can wait one breath. What is it?
